items.title: mw00/project-maya
items.excerpt: Project Maya - run GLM-5.3-Flash (321B MoE) privately on your own GPU(s), from one card to 16, NVIDIA or AMD, Linux or Windows. Engine, server, dashboard, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, quant tools.
items.summary: Project Maya lets users run GLM-5.3-Flash (321B MoE) privately on own GPUs—1 to 16 cards, NVIDIA or AMD, Linux or Windows—with engine, server, dashboard, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, and quantization tools.
items.usefulness: Could enable building Python tools for local inference if deploying quantized models on available hardware proves feasible without undisclosed dependencies.
items.to_verify: Whether the quantization tools support standard formats; actual VRAM requirements per GPU count; API compatibility depth with Claude/OpenAI clients.

items.title: How the Claude Code team does code review
items.summary: Claude Code team describes their code review practices at Anthropic, suggesting AI governance patterns for collaborative development workflows.
items.usefulness: Could inform governance policies when building Python tools with AI assistance if the post details review criteria, approval flows, or risk controls specific to AI-generated code.
items.to_verify: What specific code review criteria apply to AI-generated versus human code; whether approval patterns differ by risk class; reproducibility of review process.
